ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, with $AB=2$. $OC$ is the radius of $\odot O$, and $OC\perp AB$. Point $D$ lies on $\overset{\frown}{AC}$, and $\overset{\frown}{AD}=2\overset{\frown}{CD}$. Point $P$ is a moving point on the radius $OC$. What is the minimum value of $AP+PD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line BD, intersecting OC at point P. Draw lines OD, AP, AD.\\
Since $OC\perp AB$ and point $P$ is a movable point on the radius $OC$,\\
it follows that $AP=PB$\\
Since $DP+AP=DP+PB\ge DB$\\
the minimum value of $AP+PD$ is the length of $DB$,\\
hence, $\overset{\frown}{AC}=\overset{\frown}{CB}$, $\angle AOC=90^\circ$\\
Since $\overset{\frown}{AD}=2\overset{\frown}{CD}$\\
it follows that $\overset{\frown}{AD}=\frac{2}{3}\overset{\frown}{AC}$\\
Therefore, $\angle AOD=\frac{2}{3}\angle AOC=60^\circ$\\
Since $\overset{\frown}{AD}=\overset{\frown}{AD}$\\
it follows that $\angle ABD=30^\circ$\\
In right triangle $\triangle ADC$\\
$AB=2$, $AD=\frac{1}{2}AB=1$\\
Therefore, $BD=\sqrt{3}$\\
Hence, the minimum value of $AP+PD$ is $\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$

Since AB is a diameter, ∠ADB = 90°, so triangle ADB is a right triangle with AB as the hypotenuse. Thus BD = sqrt(AB^2 - AD^2) = sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3). Therefore the minimum value is sqrt(3).
